changes.title: Facebook's two-link-post test expanded in September: more Pages capped unless they pay for Meta One
changes.summary: Meta has run this as a test since December 2025, and in September 2026 — as Meta One for Business launched (announced September 15) — managers at more Pages and professional-mode accounts began hitting the cap: two organic posts with external links per calendar month for free, with anything past that shown as plain text rather than a clickable link. Social Media Today reported the expansion on September 17; Press Gazette reported on October 7 that news-publisher Pages are excluded for now, and priced the tiers that lift the cap: $49.99 a month for 8 link posts, $149.99 for 20, $499.99 for unlimited, while the $14.99 Essential tier adds none. Later reporting says links in comments count toward the allowance too. It is still a test, not a rule for every Page — some accounts are capped and others are not — so check your own Page's notice before planning a month of link posts around it.

changes.title: TikTok Smart+ Creative Selection pools creator videos into paid ad campaigns (announced Oct 5)
changes.summary: Announced October 5 at Advertising Week New York and reported the same week by Marketing Dive and MediaPost: Smart+ Creative Selection brings three sources of creative — an advertiser's own assets, Symphony AI-generated video, and creator content — into a single approval workflow for performance campaigns. The system surfaces recommended groups of creative matched to the campaign objective, and the advertiser decides what goes live. What TikTok has not published is the creator side of the terms: no pay rate, no revenue share, and no stated opt-in or opt-out for the creators whose videos enter the pool. Until those terms appear, a creator clip used this way is a usage-rights question — what a brand may do with your video in paid media belongs in your contract, not in an assumption from the announcement.

changes.title: Kenya's 5% withholding now comes off platform payouts — Meta from January, YouTube from September earnings
changes.summary: The 5% is not a new platform fee: it is Kenya's withholding tax on digital-content income (in law since the Finance Act 2023), and 2026 is the year the platforms began deducting it at source. Meta went first — creators were told in November 2025 that 5% would come off Facebook and Instagram payouts from January 1, 2026, shown on the monthly remittance advice. Google followed for YouTube: 5% off finalised AdSense earnings, starting with September 2026 earnings paid in October, with a verified Kenya Revenue Authority PIN due in AdSense by October 1 or payments are held. TikTok asked Kenyan creators for tax information in mid-September, but has published no rate, start date, or consequence — do not assume the 5% figure or the YouTube deadlines are TikTok's. The withheld amount is an advance against your own tax bill, credited through a withholding certificate, not a second tax on the same income.

changes.title: Meta banned TikTok and ByteDance ads on Facebook and Instagram in seven countries (Oct 8)
changes.summary: From October 8, Meta no longer sells ads or paid marketing messages to ByteDance on Facebook, Instagram, and Threads in the United States, Canada, Egypt, Indonesia, Japan, Thailand, and Vietnam — and the ban reaches third-party advertisers whose campaigns link out to TikTok or other ByteDance properties in those markets. Organic posts and mentions are not covered; this is a paid-promotion rule. Meta's stated reason is that it does not have to run ads for a competitor whose goal is to pull people off its apps. For creators and brands, a paid Meta campaign can no longer be the bridge that sends viewers to a TikTok account in those seven markets — check any cross-platform campaign's destination before it is rejected at review.

changes.title: Twitch opened Creator Sponsorships to Affiliates on Aug 20, 2026
changes.summary: Brand campaigns run through Twitch used to be a mostly Partner-only door. From August 20, Affiliates worldwide can be found by brands, invited to campaigns, and paid through the Sponsorship Dashboard in the Creator Dashboard — the same campaign pool Partners use, not a smaller Affiliate pool. The gate is paperwork, not Partner status: accept the Sponsorship Portal terms and finish the Creator Sponsorship Certification on Creator Camp for a Certified Creator badge; each brand still picks against its own criteria, and Twitch publishes no sponsorship rate. Twitch pointed to its Minecraft trial campaigns, where more than half the paid streamers were Affiliates, as the reason the door opened.

changes.title: TikTok Community Guidelines 2026H2 (effective Sep 24): bans can reach associated accounts
changes.summary: Released August 25 and in force from September 24, the new guidelines leave most content rules where they were and rewrite the enforcement side. The penalty ladder is now spelled out — warning, temporary feature or account restriction, full ban — and account status (Healthy, Fair, Severe, Banned) reflects the last 90 days, with violations expiring after 90 days and no published line between statuses. Two parts are new: optional policy training can lift eligible restrictions for certain first violations (severe violations do not qualify), and a serious violation or an attempt to dodge enforcement can now reach associated accounts — a term TikTok does not define. Undisclosed ads are no longer automatically kept off For You in this text, though other TikTok pages still say they can be pulled.

changes.title: TikTok One Pay promises campaign pay within 30 days; One Plus adds 15% on Custom Collab deals
changes.summary: On September 24 TikTok added two payment rails inside TikTok One. TikTok One Pay promises creators payment within 30 days of posting, with no fees — a direct answer to the long waits that have been the normal cost of brand work. TikTok One Plus is invite-only and pays 15% more on Custom Collab deals at no added cost to the brand. One trade report carries both moves and TikTok has not yet published the full terms in its own help pages, so treat the figures as directional until they appear inside your TikTok One account.

changes.title: Spotify Partner Program expands to 37 more markets on Oct 20, 2026
changes.summary: Announced September 17: the Spotify Partner Program — Premium video revenue plus a 50% share of ads Spotify sells into episodes — opens in 37 more markets on October 20, including Spain, Italy, Poland, Brazil, and Mexico. The eligibility bar, lowered earlier in 2026, is 3 published episodes, 2,000 consumption hours, and a 1,000 audience count in the last 30 days. Creators keep 100% of sponsorships they sell themselves. Logged here on publication of Spotify's own market list; this closes the watch slot held since October 12 — the program is not new, the map is.

changes.title: X retired Revenue Sharing on Sept 7; Original Content Rewards pays only for qualified impressions
changes.summary: X stopped new Revenue Sharing enrollments on August 7, 2026, retired the program on September 7, and opened applications for Original Content Rewards from September 8. The replacement pays on qualified impressions only: views by Premium subscribers on the Home Timeline with at least half the post visible; paid, promoted, and artificial impressions do not count. Gates: an active Premium, Premium+, or Premium Business subscription, 500 verified followers, and 500,000 verified Home Timeline impressions in the prior 90 days. Payouts run biweekly over a $30 minimum. Copied, aggregated, and lightly edited posts do not qualify, and X has published no per-impression rate — rates quoted from the old program describe a dead program.

changes.title: Facebook Content Monetization: the March 2026 originality rule can cut reach, then pay
changes.summary: Meta ended In-Stream Ads, Ads on Reels, and the Performance Bonus on August 31, 2025 and merged them into one Content Monetization program. In March 2026 it tightened the other side of the deal: content that is duplicative, or that makes only minor edits to someone else's post — borders, captions, speed changes, a logo on a repost — is treated as unoriginal, deprioritized in distribution, and a page that keeps posting mainly unoriginal work can be marked non-recommendable and demonetized. Cross-posting your own Reels is fine. Creator guides report the gate as 10,000 followers, 600,000 eligible minutes viewed in 60 days, and 5+ published videos — and only a share of raw views ever counts as eligible plays, so plan on eligible plays, not views.
